Heard Mr. P. Das, learned counsel for the applicant.

Also heard Mr. P.
Borthakur, learned Public Prosecutor for the State respondent.
This application is filed under Section 438 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, praying for granting anticipatory bail to the accused person in connection with CID Police Station Case No.06/2015, registered under Sections 120(B)/420/406 of the Indian Penal Code.
Case diary has been received and I have perused the same.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. P. Das, that the accused/applicant is innocent and not at all involved in the offence as alleged in the FIR.
Moreover, the entire allegation leveled against her is completely false, baseless and concocted.

The learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present accused/applicant is living separately from her husband since 2016 with her one child and also she is not acquainted with the facts and circumstances of this case.

She had no knowledge regarding the pendency of any case before the CID Police Station and since there is no traces of her husband since last 7 years; she was neither informed by any person nor any notice or summon to appear before the IO in respect of this instant case.
The FIR was lodged on 07.02.2015 and thereafter, application for pre-arrest bail was rejected by this Court, vide order dated 05.05.2015 passed in Page No.# 3/3 AB/1215/2015.
She came to know about filing of the case only through paper publication, which was published in local daily newspaper.
The accused/applicant has prayed for anticipatory bail, and submitted further that she is ready to co-operate with further investigation of this case, if the same is granted.

In this context, Mr. P. Borthakur, learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that the accused/applicant earlier bail prayer was rejected by this court after perusal of the Case Diary and also it cannot be accepted that she was not aware about the case.
He also submitted that several lakhs of transaction was done in her account, since 2012 to 2015 onwards.
Accordingly, the IO raised strong objections in granting bail to the accused/applicant.
Thus in this regard, custodial interrogation is hereby necessary.

After hearing the submission made by the learned Advocates of both sides as well as perusing the case diary and the earlier bail rejection order passed by this Court, I find that custodial interrogation of the accused/applicant may be necessary to unearth some more facts and accordingly, I am of the view that this is not a fit case, where, the privilege of pre-arrest bail can be granted to the accused/applicant at this stage and accordingly, the same stands rejected.
In view of above, this Anticipatory Bail application stands disposed of.
Case Diary be returned.
JUDGE
